newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel blames Lebanon for rocket attack.
newsitem.headline: Israel blames Lebanon for rocket attack.

text.p: Israel blamed Lebanon on Thursday for a cross-border rocket attack that dramatised growing tensions between the Jewish state and Lebanese guerrillas.

The Katyusha rocket slammed into western Galilee on Wednesday, the same day that the army said an Israeli soldier and three Shi'ite Amal guerrillas were killed in clashes that wounded eight Israeli soldiers.
No one was injured by the rocket. But Uri Lubrani, Israel's chief policymaker in Lebanon, told army radio: "It seems to me the Katyusha issue is a real deterioration."
"There's no doubt the responsibility for this must be placed on the government of Lebanon," he added.

The army said Israel had filed a complaint with a five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding reached in April 1996 banning pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas from firing Katyushas into Israel.
"We have a war and I say that the very country, the very Lebanon, which is a member of the committee, must take responsibility for all disturbances," Lubrani said.
Also on Wednesday, Lebanese security sources said Israeli planes twice raided suspected targets of Islamic guerrillas in south Lebanon.
Lubrani said Syria, the main power broker in Lebanon, could stop the guerrilla attacks against Israel. He said progress in peace negotiations with Syria would calm things down.

"If Syria would want to stop the activity of Hizbollah and the rest of the terrorist groups, it could. Syria apparently has no interest in doing that but the direct responsibility for activity from within Lebanon -- a Katyusha that no one has claimed responsibility for -- is the direct responsibility of the government of Lebanon," he said.
Israel and its militia allies patrol a south Lebanon occupation zone the Jewish state carved out in 1985 to prevent cross-border raids.
